objective: Exploratory census with a frozen contract: Hagemann-Mitschke term searches for the lift K4 and for the non-constant removals L-(2,2,3) and L-(2,3,3); exhaustive Hagemann-Mitschke and Day chains in the two-element clones these laws and the shadow K6 restrict to; a ternary polymorphism Mal'tsev modulo the tops for K4, L-(2,2,3), L-(2,3,3), K6 and the 4-variable product; the eight Boolean dressings of x+y+z=0 over Z3; controls with Mal'tsev laws that do not compose like cycles.
status: Closed: supported by MALTSEV-CONDITIONS-20261021-001A-E001 (exploratory; H1-H5 hold and all four controls pass; the independent check re-verified every witness table by brute force and re-decided every two-element chain with its own fixpoint; its first version compared derived equivalences as tuples against stored lists and was corrected to compare them as sets). K4 has no Mal'tsev polymorphism but has Hagemann-Mitschke terms for 3-permutability. L-(2,2,3) and L-(2,3,3) have no Hagemann-Mitschke terms for n up to 6, and their two-element block clones (all but 001, all but 011) have no Hagemann-Mitschke and no Day chain of any length; nor does the fibre clone of the shadow K6 (not exactly two ones), and K6 has no Hagemann-Mitschke terms for n = 2, 3. K4, L-(2,2,3), L-(2,3,3), K6 and the 4-variable product each have a polymorphism Mal'tsev modulo their tops, the top being the largest derived equivalence. Of the eight Boolean dressings of x+y+z=0 over Z3, only the full relation has chains. x+y+z=0 over Z6 and over Z2xZ2 have Mal'tsev polymorphisms; the Boolean neither-knot has none.
title: Census: permutability, modularity and Mal'tsev-on-tops for laws composing like cycles
